38.0.0.en: 1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, set thy face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him, 3 And say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal: 4 And I will turn thee back, and put hooks into thy jaws, and I will bring thee forth, and all thine army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed with all sorts of armour, even a great company with bucklers and shields, all of them handling swords: 5 Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya with them; all of them with shield and helmet: 6 Gomer, and all his bands; the house of Togarmah of the north quarters, and all his bands: and many people with thee. 7 Be thou prepared, and prepare for thyself, thou, and all thy company that are assembled unto thee, and be thou a guard unto them. 8 After many days thou shalt be visited: in the latter years thou shalt come into the land that is brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people, against the mountains of Israel, which have been always waste: but it is brought forth out of the nations, and they shall dwell safely all of them. 9 Thou shalt ascend and come like a storm, thou shalt be like a cloud to cover the land, thou, and all thy bands, and many people with thee. 10 Thus saith the Lord GOD; It shall also come to pass, that at the same time shall things come into thy mind, and thou shalt think an evil thought: 11 And thou shalt say, I will go up to the land of unwalled villages; I will go to them that are at rest, that dwell safely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having neither bars nor gates, 12 To take a spoil, and to take a prey; to turn thine hand upon the desolate places that are now inhabited, and upon the people that are gathered out of the nations, which have gotten cattle and goods, that dwell in the midst of the land. 13 Sheba, and Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish, with all the young lions thereof, shall say unto thee, Art thou come to take a spoil? hast thou gathered thy company to take a prey? to carry away silver and gold, to take away cattle and goods, to take a great spoil? 14 Therefore, son of man, prophesy and say unto Gog, Thus saith the Lord GOD; In that day when my people of Israel dwelleth safely, shalt thou not know it? 15 And thou shalt come from thy place out of the north parts, thou, and many people with thee, all of them riding upon horses, a great company, and a mighty army: 16 And thou shalt come up against my people of Israel, as a cloud to cover the land; it shall be in the latter days, and I will bring thee against my land, that the heathen may know me, when I shall be sanctified in thee, O Gog, before their eyes. 17 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Art thou he of whom I have spoken in old time by my servants the prophets of Israel, which prophesied in those days many years that I would bring thee against them? 18 And it shall come to pass at the same time when Gog shall come against the land of Israel, saith the Lord GOD, that my fury shall come up in my face. 19 For in my jealousy and in the fire of my wrath have I spoken, Surely in that day there shall be a great shaking in the land of Israel; 20 So that the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the heaven, and the beasts of the field, and all creeping things that creep upon the earth, and all the men that are upon the face of the earth, shall shake at my presence, and the mountains shall be thrown down, and the steep places shall fall, and every wall shall fall to the ground. 21 And I will call for a sword against him throughout all my mountains, saith the Lord GOD: every man's sword shall be against his brother. 22 And I will plead against him with pestilence and with blood; and I will rain upon him, and upon his bands, and upon the many people that are with him, an overflowing rain, and great hailstones, fire, and brimstone. 23 Thus will I magnify myself, and sanctify myself; and I will be known in the eyes of many nations, and they shall know that I am the LORD."

38.0.1.en: The prophecies against "Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal" [1], found in the two chapters [Ezek 38, 39], occupied the minds of the men of the New Testament from a very early age, especially since "Gog and Magog" are mentioned in the Book of Revelation (Rev 20:8) as representing a violent war against the Kingdom of God at the end of the ages, on the level of the whole world, which ends with the victory of truth in the end after severe tribulation. For this reason two groups of interpreters appeared. One sees Gog as a real person who bore this name, a prince over the land of Magog, who waged war against Israel returning from captivity; these interpret what is written in these two chapters in a literal way. The other group sees that what is mentioned here is a symbol representing enmity against God and resistance to the Kingdom in every age, especially at the end of the ages.

38.1.0.en: The origin of the word in the Akkadian language, gagu, means a precious ornament made of gold.

38.1.1.en: Gog, from the land of Magog, prince of Meshech and Tubal, was a symbol of idolatry with all its powers of resistance to the Kingdom of God. Perhaps the name was taken from Gyges (Guges), the head of a Lydian royal family called Mermnadae, whom the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal called "Gugu." Gyges was in the royal guard and was trusted by the king, and about the year 685 B.C. he killed his master of the house rival to the Heraclid dynasty, and seized the throne of the kingdom of Lydia. He was very rich and offered great gifts to the temple of Apollo at Delphi. But he rebelled against the Greek cities in Asia Minor. In his old age the Cimmerian invaders (Gimirra, Cimmerians) defeated him, but he rose against them and defeated them with the help of Assyria. But when Gyges turned back and helped Egypt to revolt against Assyria, this deed provoked the king of Assyria, who set the Cimmerians against him to invade the kingdom of Lydia again about the year 645 B.C., in which the king was killed, leaving his son Ardys as his successor.

38.1.2.en: Some see that Gog was connected with Gaga mentioned in the Amarna tablets, a distortion of the word Gaga, a barren province of Armenia and Cappadocia. The people of this region passed into the sea of oblivion, so the name Gog came to bear a barbaric meaning, that is, it became the memory of a barbarian people whom time has folded away and everyone has forgotten.

38.1.3.en: Others see that Gog came from a Babylonian god called Gaga, or from the ruler of a city, Sabi, called Gagi, to which Ashurbanipal king of Assyria referred.

38.2.0.en: The name of a people descended from Magog, the second son of Japheth (Gen 10:12; 1 Chr 1:5), or the name of the land they inhabited, which seems to have been in the far north.

38.2.1.en: Since it is mentioned here that Gog, the prince of Meshech and Tubal, reigns over Magog, and that he led a violent campaign against Israel after its return, bringing it from the north in alliance with Gomer and the house of Togarmah, it is seen that Magog is a people (or a land) in the north of Palestine, not far from Meshech and Tubal, their homeland in the northeast of Cilicia (Cilicia), as is stated in the Assyrian documents.

38.2.2.en: The Syrians called the land of the Tatars Magog, and the Arabs also called the land lying between the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea Magog, but the majority accepted what is in Josephus, that the Magog are the Scythian tribes. Herodotus referred to these tribes as belonging to the north of Crimea, and they were known for their violent, fierce raids in Asia and in other places: in the seventh century B.C. they marched from Mount Qaf and conquered Sardis, the capital of Lydia, and also defeated Cyaxares king of Media and reached Egypt, where King Psammetichus gave them a sum of money and sent them away from his country. The prophet Ezekiel described them as a people skilled in horsemanship and the use of the bow, and this description matches what is in the history of the Greeks. But since we have seen that Gog king of Magog most probably refers to Gyges king of Lydia, this does not apply to these tribes, unless the word "Magog" here carries a symbolic meaning of Gog's violence, his passion for attacking others and his ferocity in fighting.

38.3.0.en: Since the names "Gog and Magog" are mentioned in the Book of Revelation (Rev 20:8-10) as representing a war that includes armies from the four corners of the earth under satanic leadership, to deceive mankind and to stir up war against the saints at the end of the ages, some have interpreted what is said in (Ezek 38-39) to mean that Gog and Magog are not to be understood in the literal historical sense but in the symbolic sense.

38.3.1.en: a. Some see that Gog is a symbol of the Babylonians, or the Scythians, or Cambyses king of the Persians, or Alexander the Great, or Antiochus the Great, or Antiochus Epiphanes, etc...

38.3.2.en: b. Others see that Gog king of Magog refers to a military alliance and bloc against the people of God.

38.3.3.en: c. Others see that what is said about Gog does not refer to particular historical events but symbolizes the spiritual war between the devil, who controls many kingdoms, and God, who reigns over the saints; and that, despite the powers and violence the devil uses, the victory belongs to truth.

38.4.0.en: d. Some interpret Gog and Magog as a symbol of Russia, depending on the word "Rosh" as an ancient name for Russia. They interpret the word Meshech as a symbol of Moscow, the capital of Russia, and Tubal as a symbol of Tubalt, also in Russia. They see that Persia (Iran), Cush (Ethiopia) and Put (Libya) [5]... as though the prophecy points to sufferings that the Church passes through at the end of the ages, from the movement of several peoples led by Russia. As for Togarmah, they interpret it as eastern Germany (Germani). This military movement is on the level of kings and peoples from every direction, but most of it comes from the north, for he says: "And thou shalt come from thy place out of the north parts, thou, and many people with thee, all of them riding upon horses, a great company, and a mighty army: and thou shalt come up against my people of Israel, as a cloud to cover the land; it shall be in the latter days" [15-16]. But these peoples include kingdoms such as Ethiopia, Libya, Sheba, Dedan and Tarshish!!!

38.4.1.en: As for the word "Israel," some have seen it as a war directed toward Jerusalem, but the majority see that the word "Israel" here means the believing people of God; the war is directed against the Church, not a particular region, for the Book of Revelation says: "And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them" (Rev 20:7-9).

38.5.0.en: As for the state of the Church at that time, it is said of it: "Thus saith the Lord GOD; It shall also come to pass, that at the same time shall things come into thy mind, and thou shalt think an evil thought: And thou shalt say, I will go up to the land of unwalled villages; I will go to them that are at rest, that dwell safely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having neither bars nor gates" [10-11]. It is as though the universal war at the end of the ages against the Church is not founded on the Church provoking the enemy, but the enemy sees her calm and safe, and thinks she dwells without a wall to protect her, nor a bar to hinder the enemies from her, nor gates to shut her doors, open and easy for plunder and spoil. He does not know that the Lord Himself is the wall of the believer, and it is He who embraces him and protects him within Himself, shutting him in with heavenly doors that the devil and all his hosts cannot open.

38.5.1.en: But it is feared that it will be so, that the believers in the last days will be like those who are in an open land without a wall, bars or gates, where the Lord says: "And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many. And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold" (Mt 24:11-12), "For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. Behold, I have told you before" (Mt 24:24-25).

38.5.3.en: *A dangerous enemy who spares no effort to destroy Your Kingdom!

38.5.4.en: But You, O God, are greater than every enemy!

38.5.5.en: *I am not a party to the battle; I hide in You, so I overcome and triumph by You!

38.5.6.en: The enemy's war began from the creation of man, and its blaze increases until the Antichrist comes!

38.5.7.en: The war grows very fierce, so that, if it were possible, even the elect would be deceived!

38.5.9.en: Be of good cheer; I have overcome the world!

38.5.10.en: The enemy is dangerous, but You are the Giver of victory!

38.5.11.en: *You did not deceive us, but affirmed to us the severity of the war and its increase, and You gave us Yourself, the mystery of overcoming and victory!

39.0.0.en: 1 "Therefore, thou son of man, prophesy against Gog, and say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal: 2 And I will turn thee back, and leave but the sixth part of thee, and will cause thee to come up from the north parts, and will bring thee upon the mountains of Israel: 3 And I will smite thy bow out of thy left hand, and will cause thine arrows to fall out of thy right hand. 4 Thou shalt fall upon the mountains of Israel, thou, and all thy bands, and the people that is with thee: I will give thee unto the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the beasts of the field to be devoured. 5 Thou shalt fall upon the open field: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord GOD. 6 And I will send a fire on Magog, and among them that dwell carelessly in the isles: and they shall know that I am the LORD. 7 So will I make my holy name known in the midst of my people Israel; and I will not let them pollute my holy name any more: and the heathen shall know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel."

39.0.1.en: He returned to affirm the final destruction of Gog, as a sign of the final victory of the Kingdom of God over the kingdom of darkness.

39.1.0.en: It is wonderful that God, when He declares His opposition to Gog, says: "I will turn thee back... and will cause thee to come up from the north parts, and will bring thee upon the mountains of Israel" [2]. It is as though what Gog does of violence against God and His children is not hidden from God, but is with His permission, so that God may be glorified in His people.

39.2.0.en: Before He permits his destruction, the Lord smites his bow and makes his arrows fall; for God did not first condemn Satan, but first broke his authority, when He broke his evil weapons on the Cross, so as to give His children the opportunity to overcome him. As for the falling of Gog upon the mountains of Israel, he and all his army and the peoples with him [4], it is a declaration of the place of the battle, the firm mountains of the believers, that is, their hearts, which have become like rock, unshaken before the temptations of the devil. As the Lord Christ defeated the devil on the mountain, so we enter with Him into a battle within the heart and break him, and he has no place in us. He wanted to reign over the heart, and there we cast him down by divine grace under our feet.

39.2.1.en: Gog falls and becomes a prey for the believers who rise by grace like birds, soaring in the heavenly places, and who train for spiritual warfare and become like ravenous beasts, so that sin cannot stand before them. As for the fire that burns him, it is the fire of the divine Spirit dwelling in us, who purifies us from every sin and weakness and burns every evil and satanic work. This is the secret of our victory over Satan: the lifting of our life in Christ Jesus toward the heavenly places, and training for striving without slackness, our hearts aflame with the fiery Spirit of God.

39.3.0.en: 8 "Behold, it is come, and it is done, saith the Lord GOD; this is the day whereof I have spoken. 9 And they that dwell in the cities of Israel shall go forth, and shall set on fire and burn the weapons, both the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves, and the spears, and they shall burn them with fire seven years: 10 So that they shall take no wood out of the field, neither cut down any out of the forests; for they shall burn the weapons with fire: and they shall spoil those that spoiled them, and rob those that robbed them, saith the Lord GOD. 11 And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will give unto Gog a place there of graves in Israel, the valley of the passengers on the east of the sea: and it shall stop the noses of the passengers: and there shall they bury Gog and all his multitude: and they shall call it The valley of Hamongog. 12 And seven months shall the house of Israel be burying of them, that they may cleanse the land. 13 Yea, all the people of the land shall bury them; and it shall be to them a renown the day that I shall be glorified, saith the Lord GOD. 14 And they shall sever out men of continual employment, passing through the land to bury with the passengers those that remain upon the face of the earth, to cleanse it: after the end of seven months shall they search. 15 And the passengers that pass through the land, when any seeth a man's bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamongog. 16 And also the name of the city shall be Hamonah. Thus shall they cleanse the land."

39.4.0.en: The goal of the destruction of the devil and his hosts is the entrance of the believers into a state of final peace. For when the devil is cast into the eternal fire, the believers enter the eternal Kingdom, and thereafter have no need of weapons, where there is neither enemy nor war. "They shall set on fire and burn the weapons, both the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves, and the spears, and they shall burn them with fire seven years" [9]. That is, they burn every kind of weapon, and to the end, where the number 7 signifies perfection.

39.5.0.en: Where the believers overcome, the demons are defeated and there is no place for uncleanness, for the people bury the corpses in "the valley of the passengers" (the valley of Abarim) [11], and the land is cleansed of these defiled corpses; and the valley of Abarim is called "the valley of the multitude of Gog" [11, 15], and the city is called "Hamonah," that is, multitude, for the multitude that follows Gog, or the demons, is buried in it.

39.6.0.en: "Abarim" in Hebrew means "what has crossed over," and it is a chain of mountains east of the Jordan, called "Abarim" because they are across the river, and it lies outside the Holy Land. The prophet Jeremiah mentioned it in his enumeration of the mountains in Syria after Lebanon and Bashan (Jer 22:20), and the Hebrews camped in it before they crossed the river Arnon (Num 21:11), then it was given to the sons of Reuben (Num 32:2-37). The mountains of Abarim extend from the valley of Kafrain in the north to the valley of Zarqa Ma'in and the valley of Hasa in the south. Abarim has peaks, among them Nebo, Hosha and Ajlun, and the prophet Moses stood on Mount Nebo and saw the Promised Land (Num 27:12; Deut 32:49; 34:1).

39.6.1.en: Perhaps the Lord wanted to declare, by the burying of Gog's multitude in Abarim, the victory of the children of God while they are still in the world, before they cross over to the other life. They stand like Moses on the summit of Nebo and see the heavenly Jerusalem and perceive the divine glories, so they are purified by the Holy Spirit from every uncleanness and overcome all the powers of darkness...

39.6.2.en: The work of the believer in this life, as this chapter affirms, is to bury the multitude of Gog, that is, to bury the demons of darkness, so that they have no life in his heart.

39.7.0.en: He says: "When any seeth a man's bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamongog" [15]. By "sign" he means a mark. When the believer sees the traces of the devil's falls, he makes the sign of the Cross, which is the sign of victory, until the devil is buried completely in this valley and has no place in it any more. Our message is to hold fast to the sign of victory and triumph until we are crowned in the end.

39.8.0.en: 17 "And, thou son of man, thus saith the Lord GOD; Speak unto every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh, and drink blood. 18 Ye shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, of lambs, and of goats, of bullocks, all of them fatlings of Bashan. 19 And ye shall eat fat till ye be full, and drink blood till ye be drunken, of my sacrifice which I have sacrificed for you. 20 Thus ye shall be filled at my table with horses and chariots, with mighty men, and with all men of war, saith the Lord GOD. 21 And I will set my glory among the heathen, and all the heathen shall see my judgment that I have executed, and my hand that I have laid upon them. 22 So the house of Israel shall know that I am the LORD their God from that day and forward. 23 And the heathen shall know that the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity: because they trespassed against me, therefore hid I my face from them, and gave them into the hand of their enemies: so fell they all by the sword. 24 According to their uncleanness and according to their transgressions have I done unto them, and hid my face from them. 25 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Now will I bring again the captivity of Jacob, and have mercy upon the whole house of Israel, and will be jealous for my holy name; 26 After that they have borne their shame, and all their trespasses whereby they have trespassed against me, when they dwelt safely in their land, and none made them afraid. 27 When I have brought them again from the people, and gathered them out of their enemies' lands, and am sanctified in them in the sight of many nations; 28 Then shall they know that I am the LORD their God, which caused them to be led into captivity among the heathen: but I have gathered them unto their own land, and have left none of them any more there. 29 Neither will I hide my face any more from them: for I have poured out my spirit upon the house of Israel, saith the Lord GOD."

39.8.1.en: Perhaps in this conclusion he meant to make clear the difference between the falling of the multitude of Gog in the Holy Land and the great sacrifice in which many of His children died: for the multitude of Gog end by being utterly destroyed in the eternal fire, while the children of God are disciplined for a time until they repent and return to God, and His name is glorified in them.

39.9.0.en: And perhaps by the great feast here on the holy mountains he meant the slaying of the multitude of Gog who perished... In any case, the Lord made completely clear the return of His children to Him by repentance in surpassing peace, and the Lord's jealousy for them for the sake of His holy name, so that He no longer hides His face from them, for He has poured out His Spirit upon them [29]. With this the Book of Ezekiel reaches its goal. The glory of God departed from His people and His temple because of sin, and now by discipline they returned to Him repentant, so the glory of God returned to them and His name was sanctified in them.

39.9.1.en: And now this divine glory is declared in the following chapters through the new temple, the new city and the new people.

39.9.3.en: * Gog, the symbol of Satan, wants to destroy the Kingdom of God completely, and his war grows very fierce at the end of times!

39.9.4.en: But he is shattered, he and all his hosts, on the holy mountain!

39.9.5.en: The enemy falls slain under the feet of the believers, while they are lifted up to the very heavens.

39.9.6.en: Instead of reigning over the heart, my heart becomes a tomb for him!

39.9.7.en: Instead of wounding me with his arrows, he dies by his own weapon!

39.9.8.en: *When shall I overcome by the sign of Your Cross, O Savior?

39.9.9.en: When will the war end, and I be lifted up into the bosom of Your Father, where I shall not need a weapon, for there will be no enemy any more!

39.9.10.en: There I shall see the enemy descend to the fire of hell eternally, and Your believers enjoying Your glory and Your surpassing peace!
